chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all together, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Hamath al-Thimali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying:

O Thabit, indeed Allah the Exalted had timed this matter for the year seventy. But when al-Husayn was killed, Allah's anger intensified, so He delayed it until the year one hundred and forty. We told you of that, and you announced it and uncovered the veil of concealment, so after that Allah did not assign a specific time for this matter to us. And Allah blots out and establishes what He pleases, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
Abu Hamza said: I narrated that to Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It was so.'

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab)
key_terms.الْأَمْرَ: the matter (referring to the rise of the Qa'im)
key_terms.يَمْحُو وَيُثْبِتُ: He blots out and establishes (divine decree)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of the delay in the timing of the Imam's rise in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir reveals that the specific timing of the Qa'im's appearance was originally decreed for 70 AH but was deferred to 140 AH following the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn, an event that intensified divine wrath. Upon the companions' disclosure of this secret, the precise date was concealed from them, illustrating the theological principle of *al-ghayb al-mutlaq* (absolute hiddenness) where Allah blots out and establishes as He wills. This event underscores the Shia belief in the dynamic nature of divine decree (*taqdir*) in response to human actions and the ultimate preservation of the exact time in *Umm al-Kitab*.
